68: static void __attribute__((naked, noreturn))
69: bk7258_secondary_enter(uintptr_t idle_top __attribute__((unused)),
70:                        uintptr_t idle_base __attribute__((unused)))
71: {
72:   __asm__ volatile
73:     (
74:       "msr psp, r0\n"
75: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
76:       "msr psplim, r1\n"
77: #endif
78:       "mrs r1, control\n"
79:       "orr r1, r1, #2\n"
80:       "msr control, r1\n"
81:       "isb sy\n"
82:       "b bk7258_secondary_idle\n"
83:     );

94:   bk7258_cpu_private_initialize(false);
95:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_PRIVATE);
96:   bk7258_irqinitialize_secondary();
97:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ);
98:   if (bk7258_mbox_secondary_init() < 0)
99:     {
100:       PANIC();
101:     }
102: 
103:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX);
104: 
105:   tcb = current_task(1);
106:   idle_top = ((uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr + tcb->adj_stack_size) & ~7u;
107:   bk7258_secondary_enter(idle_top, (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr);

114:     (
115:       "cpsid i\n"
116:       "movs r0, #1\n"
117:       "ldr r1, =0x20000000\n"
118:       "str r0, [r1]\n"
119:       "ldr r0, =__secondary_boot_stack_base\n"
120:       "msr msplim, r0\n"
121:       "b bk7258_secondary_boot\n"
122:     );

125: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
126: {
127:   clock_t started;
128:   uint32_t control;
129:   uint32_t status;
130: 
131:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ENTER);
132: 
133:   if (cpu != 1 || this_cpu() != 0)
134:     {
135:       return -EINVAL;
136:     }
137: 
138:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
139:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, status);
140:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
141:   if ((status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_POWER_DOWN) != 0 ||
142:       !bk7258_mbox_smp_ready())
143:     {
144:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 prerequisite failed: status=%08lx mbox=%u\n",
145:              (unsigned long)status, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
146:       PANIC();
147:     }
148: 
149:   bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
150:   control = getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
151:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
152:   if ((control & BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE) != 0 ||
153:       (status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_RESET) != 0)
154:     {
155:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 reset hold failed: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx\n",
156:              (unsigned long)control, (unsigned long)status);
157:       PANIC();
158:     }
159: 
160:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_HELD);
161:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, control);
162:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, status);
163: 
164:   atomic_set(&g_cpu2_online, 0);
165:   bk7258_smp_prepare_boot();
166:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0);
167:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1);
168:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL, BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_MASK,
169:               BK7258_CPU2_RXEVT_SEL |
170:               (((uintptr_t)__secondary_vectors_start >> 8) <<
171:                BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_SHIFT));
172:   UP_DMB();
173:   UP_DSB();
174:   bk7258_cpu2_release_reset();
175:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_RELEASED);
176:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
177:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
178: 
179:   started = clock_systime_ticks();
180:   while (atomic_read_acquire(&g_cpu2_online) == 0 ||
181:          !bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
182:     {
183:       if (atomic_read_acquire(&g_cpu2_online) != 0 &&
184:           bk7258_smp_boot_ping(1) == OK)
185:         {
186:           bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ONLINE);
187:           while (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete() &&
188:                  clock_systime_ticks() - started <
189:                    BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_TIMEOUT)
190:             {
191:               __asm__ volatile("wfe");
192:             }
193:         }
194: 
195:       if (clock_systime_ticks() - started >= BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_TIMEOUT)
196:         {
197:           bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
198:           bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
199:           bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0));
200:           bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1));
201:           bk7258_boottrace_detail(4,
202:                                   getreg32(BK7258_MBOX0_BASE + 0xe0u));
203:           bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
204:           syslog(LOG_ERR,
205:                  "CPU2 online timeout: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx route=%08lx/%08lx ch2=%08lx\n",
206:                  (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL),
207:                  (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS),
208:                  (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0),
209:                  (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1),
210:                  (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX0_BASE + 0xe0u));
211:           PANIC();
212:         }
213:     }
214: 
215:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IPI_DONE);
216:   return OK;
217: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 raw Mailbox SMP IPI.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <assert.h>
8: #include <errno.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: #include <strings.h>
11: 
12: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
13: #include <nuttx/atomic.h>
14: #include <nuttx/sched.h>
15: 
16: #include "arm_internal.h"
17: #include "sched/sched.h"
18: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
19: #include "bk7258_smp.h"
20: 
21: #define BK7258_IPI_SCHED        (1u << 0)
22: #define BK7258_IPI_CALL         (1u << 1)
23: #define BK7258_IPI_BOOT_TEST    (1u << 2)
24: #define BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT  1024
25: 
26: static atomic_t g_ipi_pending[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
27: static atomic_t g_ipi_kicked[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
28: static atomic_t g_boot_seen[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
29: 
30: static int bk7258_smp_kick(int cpu, uint32_t pending)
31: {
32:   uint32_t data[2] = {BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK, 0};
33:   int expected = 0;
34:   int retry;
35: 
36:   if ((unsigned int)cpu >= CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS || cpu == this_cpu())
37:     {
38:       return -EINVAL;
39:     }
40: 
41:   atomic_or_release(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], pending);
42:   if (!atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], &expected, 1))
43:     {
44:       return OK;
45:     }
46: 
47:   UP_DMB();
48:   for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
49:     {
50:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
51: 
52:       if (ret == OK)
53:         {
54:           return OK;
55:         }
56: 
57:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
58:         {
59:           return ret;
60:         }
61: 
62:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
63:     }
64: 
65:   return -ETIMEDOUT;
66: }
67: 
68: void bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(int irq, void *context, uint32_t command)
69: {
70:   int cpu = this_cpu();
71: 
72:   if (command != BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
73:     {
74:       return;
75:     }
76: 
77:   for (;;)
78:     {
79:       uint32_t pending = atomic_xchg_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
80: 
81:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_CALL) != 0)
82:         {
83:           nxsched_smp_call_handler(irq, context, NULL);
84:         }
85: 
86:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_SCHED) != 0)
87:         {
88:           nxsched_process_delivered(cpu);
89:         }
90: 
91:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_BOOT_TEST) != 0)
92:         {
93:           atomic_set_release(&g_boot_seen[cpu], 1);
94:         }
95: 
96:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
97:       UP_DMB();
98:       if (atomic_read_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu]) == 0)
99:         {
100:           break;
101:         }
102: 
103:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 1);
104:     }
105: }
106: 
107: int up_send_smp_sched(int cpu)
108: {
109:   int ret = bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_SCHED);
110: 
111:   if (ret < 0)
112:     {
113:       PANIC();
114:     }
115: 
116:   return ret;
117: }
118: 
119: void up_send_smp_call(cpu_set_t cpuset)
120: {
121:   int cpu;
122: 
123:   for (; cpuset != 0; cpuset &= ~(1u << cpu))
124:     {
125:       cpu = ffs((int)cpuset) - 1;
126:       if (cpu != this_cpu() && bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_CALL) < 0)
127:         {
128:           PANIC();
129:         }
130:     }
131: }
132: 
133: void bk7258_smp_prepare_boot(void)
134: {
135:   int cpu;
136: 
137:   for (cpu = 0; cpu < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; cpu++)
138:     {
139:       atomic_set(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
140:       atomic_set(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
141:       atomic_set(&g_boot_seen[cpu], 0);
142:     }
143: }
144: 
145: void bk7258_smp_boot_notify(void)
146: {
147:   if (bk7258_smp_kick(0, BK7258_IPI_BOOT_TEST) < 0)
148:     {
149:       PANIC();
150:     }
151: }
152: 
153: bool bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete(void)
154: {
155:   return atomic_read_acquire(&g_boot_seen[0]) != 0 &&
156:          atomic_read_acquire(&g_boot_seen[1]) != 0;
157: }
158: 
159: int bk7258_smp_boot_ping(int cpu)
160: {
161:   return bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_BOOT_TEST);
162: }

229: 
230:   mbox_clear_errors(cpu);
231:   sidreg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_SID : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_SID;
232:   rdata0 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA0 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA0;
233:   rdata1 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA1 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA1;
234: 
235:   while ((bk7258_mbox_rx_status() & 2u) == 0)
236:     {
237:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
238:       uint32_t address;
239:       uint32_t length;
240:       uint8_t source;
241: 
242:       if (cpu == 0)
243:         {
244:           mbox_process_desc();
245:         }
246: 
247:       desc = cpu == 0 ? mbox_alloc_desc() : NULL;
248:       if (cpu == 0 && desc == NULL)
249:         {
250:           g_stats.descriptor_full++;
251:           break;
252:         }
253: 
254:       source = getreg32(sidreg) & 0x0fu;
255:       address = getreg32(rdata0);
256:       length = getreg32(rdata1);
257: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
258:       if (length == 0)
259:         {
260:           if (source == (uint8_t)(2 - cpu))
261:             {
262:               bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(irq, context, address);
263:             }
264:           else
265:             {
266:               if (cpu == 0)
267:                 {
268:                   g_stats.bad_source++;
269:                 }
270:             }
271: 
272:           continue;
273:         }
274: #endif
275: 
276:       if (cpu != 0)
277:         {
278:           continue;
279:         }
280: 
281:       if (!mbox_valid_envelope(source, address, length))
282:         {
283:           continue;
284:         }
285: 
286:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
287:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
288:              sizeof(desc->message));
289:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
290:       desc->used = true;
291:       g_stats.rx_messages++;
292:       mbox_process_desc();
293:     }
294: 
295:   if (cpu == 0)
296:     {
297:       mbox_process_desc();
298:     }
299: 
300:   return OK;
301: }
302: 
303: void bk7258_mbox_set_callback(bk7258_mbox_callback_t callback)
304: {
305:   g_callback = callback;
306: }
307: 
308: void bk7258_mbox_kick_rx(void)
309: {
310:   irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();
311: 
312:   (void)bk7258_mbox_irq(0, NULL, NULL);
313:   up_irq_restore(flags);
314: }
315: 
316: void bk7258_mbox_discard_deferred(void)
317: {
318:   unsigned int i;
319: 
320:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
321:     {
322:       if (g_rx_desc[i].used && g_processing_order != 0 &&
323:           (int32_t)(g_rx_desc[i].order - g_processing_order) < 0 &&
324:           !mbox_priority_message(&g_rx_desc[i].message))
325:         {
326:           g_rx_desc[i].used = false;
327:         }
328:     }
329: }
330: 
331: void bk7258_mbox_get_stats(struct bk7258_mbox_stats *stats)
332: {
333:   irqstate_t flags;
334: 
335:   if (stats == NULL)
336:     {
337:       return;
338:     }
339: 
340:   flags = up_irq_save();
341:   *stats = g_stats;
342:   up_irq_restore(flags);
343: }
344: 
345: int bk7258_mbox_init(void)
346: {
347:   int ret;
348: 
349:   if (g_mbox_ready)
350:     {
351:       return OK;
352:     }
353: 
354:   memset(g_rx_desc, 0, sizeof(g_rx_desc));
355:   g_rx_order = 0;
356:   g_processing_order = 0;
357:   memset(&g_stats, 0, sizeof(g_stats));
358: 
359:   /* CPU1 owns channel 1 and FIFO entries 2..4.  Install the callback and
360:    * descriptors before enabling the route; pre-existing FIFO entries are
361:    * then processed normally instead of being blindly discarded.
362:    */
363: 
364:   putreg32(2u | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_INT_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN |
365:             BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN,
366:             BK7258_MBOX_CH1_CFG);
367:   putreg32(1u | (3u << 1), BK7258_MBOX_CH1_FIFO_CFG);
368: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
369:   putreg32(5u | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_INT_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN |
370:             BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN,
371:             BK7258_MBOX_CH2_CFG);
372:   putreg32(1u | (3u << 1), BK7258_MBOX_CH2_FIFO_CFG);
373: #endif
374:   modifyreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CTRL, 0, 1u << 2);
375:   mbox_clear_errors(0);
376: 
377:   ret = irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX, bk7258_mbox_irq, NULL);
378:   if (ret < 0)
379:     {
380:       return ret;
381:     }
382: 
383:   g_mbox_ready = true;
384: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
385:   g_mbox_smp_ready = true;
386: #endif
387:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1, 0, 1u << 31);
388:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX);
389:   return OK;
390: }

393: {
394: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
395:   return g_mbox_ready && g_mbox_smp_ready;
396: #else
397:   return false;
398: #endif
399: }

532: ### 6.3 CPU ID
533: 
534: 原厂 AP 使用每核私有 DTCM地址 `0x20000000` 保存 AP逻辑核 ID。OpenVela采用：
535: 
536: ```text
537: 物理CPU1私有 0x20000000 = NuttX CPU0
538: 物理CPU2私有 0x20000000 = NuttX CPU1
539: ```
540: 
541: `up_cpu_index()` 直接读取该word。primary在任何 per-CPU/NuttX atomic调用前写0；
542: secondary在任何NuttX API前写1。必须实板验证两核看到的是私有实例，不是共享word。
543: 
544: ### 6.4 内存、secondary vector和栈
545: 
546: 分区保持：
547: 
548: ```text
549: AP_SPINLOCK  0x28000000..0x2800ffff
550: AP_RAM       0x28010000..0x28063fff
551: CP_RAM       0x28064000..0x2809f6ff
552: PWR_MNG      0x2809f700..0x2809f7ff
553: SWAP         0x2809f800..0x2809ffff
554: ```
555: 
556: CPU2不增加Flash/RAM分区。链接脚本增加：
557: 
558: - `SPINLOCK` MEMORY，绝不加入heap。
559: - 512字节对齐的 `.bk_secondary_vectors`。
560: - 只用于reset早期的CPU2 bootstrap stack。
561: - 两份静态 interrupt stack，或等价的每核固定中断栈区域。
562: - 全部边界和对齐 `ASSERT`。
563: 
564: secondary vector：
565: 
566: ```text
567: word 0: CPU2 bootstrap MSP top
568: word 1: bk7258_secondary_start | 1
569: ```
570: 
571: CPU2 boot offset寄存器只保存地址高24位，至少要求256字节对齐；统一采用512字节以
572: 满足VTOR约束。secondary vector不包含primary image offset `0x100` 的BK legacy magic。
573: 
574: `up_cpu_idlestack()` 应像RP2040一样调用 `up_create_stack()`，初始化logical CPU1 idle
575: TCB。还必须分配 `CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS * INTSTACK_SIZE` 对齐空间并实现
576: `uintptr_t up_get_intstackbase(int cpu)`；公共ARM实现只覆盖UP构建，ARMv8-M任务初始状态
577: 会调用该hook。CPU2 reset后先用bootstrap MSP；进入NuttX前将PSP切到idle TCB stack
578: top，调用 `arm_initialize_stack()` 安装本核MSP/MSPLIM interrupt stack。两个核不得共用
579: MSP。

581: ### 6.5 CPU2启动
582: 
583: `up_cpu_start(1)`：
584: 
585: ```text
586: 校验cpu==1且当前为logical CPU0
587:   -> 确认CP的OpenVela CPU2 power-only hold和domain readback均为ON
588:   -> 确认480 MHz契约和channel 2已配置
589:   -> 发布idle PSP、interrupt MSP、runtime VTOR
590:   -> 清boot stage/online flag，DMB/DSB
591:   -> CPU2保持reset时清route/pending
592:   -> CPU2_RXEVT_SEL=1
593:   -> CPU2_OFFSET=secondary_vector>>8
594:   -> cpu2_release_reset()（极性已由run-status/实板验证）
595:   -> 有界等待online和双向IPI自检
596: ```
597: 
598: 超时建议500 ms，输出CPU2 control、run status、route、NVIC、Mailbox channel 2、boot
599: stage和当前频率readback，然后panic。不能只返回错误后继续 `nx_bringup()`。
600: 
601: `bk7258_secondary_start()` 只初始化每核私有状态：
602: 
603: - logical ID、FPU CP10/11和barrier。
604: - 与primary一致的SAU/MPU/VTOR。

613:

615: 初始化第二个SysTick或重置全局Mailbox FIFO。

617: ### 6.6 每核MPU/NVIC
618: 
619: MPU、SAU、NVIC、VTOR、SysTick和FPU控制均为每核私有。CPU2必须安装与CPU1相同的：
620: 
621: - AP Flash RO/X。
622: - AP RAM RW/XN/shareable。
623: - `AP_SPINLOCK` RW/XN/non-cacheable/shareable。
624: - CP共享窗口和Mailbox UART override。
625: - PSRAM 16 MiB RW/XN/non-cacheable。
626: - peripheral Device/XN。
627: 
628: 当前 CPU1 使用7个 MPU region；增加 AP_SPINLOCK 后至少需要8个，启动时继续读
629: `MPU_TYPE.DREGION`并 fail-stop。CPU2不能重复probe或初始化PSRAM allocator。
630: 
631: 全局NuttX IRQ table只由primary初始化一次。CPU2只初始化私有NVIC和CPU2 route：
632: 
633: ```text
634: CPU1 IRQ EN0/EN1: 0x44010088 / 0x4401008c
635: CPU2 IRQ EN0/EN1: 0x44010090 / 0x44010094
636: ```
637: 
638: 首版只有CPU2 Mailbox IPI路由到CPU2。GPIO、PWM、I2C、QSPI、camera、Wi-Fi和其他
639: 有状态外设仍由logical CPU0 owner。

641: ## 7. Mailbox IPI与CP transport共存
642: 
643: ### 7.1 物理channel
644: 
645: | channel | owner | FIFO |
646: | ---: | --- | --- |
647: | 0 | CPU0/CP | start 0, length 2 |
648: | 1 | CPU1/AP primary | start 2, length 3 |
649: | 2 | CPU2/AP secondary | start 5, length 3 |
650: 
651: 沿用原厂消息分类：
652: 
653: ```text
654: data[1] != 0: pointer + length envelope，进入CP/AP logical transport
655: data[1] == 0: AP内部raw command，进入SMP IPI handler
656: ```
657: 
658: CPU2不处理CP PWC、heartbeat、Wi-Fi或Mailbox UART envelope。CP transport始终由
659: logical CPU0负责。
660: 
661: ### 7.2 当前初始化路径的改造
662: 
663: 当前 physical Mailbox 已在 `arm_serialinit()` 中经：

668: bk7258_mailbox_start()
669: ```
670:

672: 
673: 1. primary physical start一次性配置channel 1和2 FIFO，不能在CPU2 online后soft reset。
674: 2. 全局 `irq_attach(79, ...)` 只执行一次；CPU2复用共享NuttX IRQ handler table，但启用

676: 3. ISR按 `up_cpu_index()` 选择本核physical channel。

678: 5. shared transport状态从仅 `up_irq_save()` 改为SMP spinlock，或严格固定到CPU0。

680: ### 7.3 NuttX SMP hooks
681: 
682: 实现：
683: 
684: ```c
685: int up_send_smp_sched(int cpu);
686: void up_send_smp_call(cpu_set_t cpuset);
687: ```
688: 
689: raw command采用pending bitmap合并 `SCHED`、`CALL`和 `PM`。发送前DMB，ISR读取并清
690: pending后DMB，然后调用：
691: 
692: ```c
693: nxsched_smp_call_handler(irq, context, arg);
694: nxsched_process_delivered(this_cpu());
695: ```
696: 
697: FIFO full不能静默丢失。采用“shared pending bit + kick”语义：消息只负责唤醒，真实
698: 工作由pending bit保持；如果目标已有未处理kick，不重复占FIFO。发送失败需要有界重试、

<thinking>**Investigating atomic backend and spinlock behavior**</thinking>
Mailbox numbering in the current raw path is internally consistent with the silicon-wide IDs used by Armino: logical CPU0 sends from physical mailbox channel 1 to destination 2, and logical CPU1 sends from channel 2 to destination 1. 111:   uint32_t rcv;

113:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_RDY))

116:   __asm__ volatile ("sev");

119:     __asm__ volatile ("wfe");

175:  * Name: up_cpu_start
176:  *
177:  * Description:
178:  *   In an SMP configuration, only one CPU is initially active (CPU 0).
179:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion of
180:  *   the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal multitasking,
181:  *   the additional CPUs would be started by calling this function.
182:  *
183:  *   Each CPU is provided the entry point to its IDLE task when started.  A
184:  *   TCB for each CPU's IDLE task has been initialized and placed in the
185:  *   CPU's g_assignedtasks[cpu] list.  No stack has been allocated or
186:  *   initialized.
187:  *
188:  *   The OS initialization logic calls this function repeatedly until each
189:  *   CPU has been started, 1 through (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
190:  *
191:  * Input Parameters:
192:  *   cpu - The index of the CPU being started.  This will be a numeric
193:  *         value in the range of one to (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
194:  *         (CPU 0 is already active)
195:  *
196:  * Returned Value:
197:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
198:  *
199:  ****************************************************************************/

201: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
202: {
203:   int i;
204:   struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(cpu);
205:   uint32_t core1_boot_msg[5];
206: 
207:   DPRINTF("cpu=%d\n", cpu);
208: 
209: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION
210:   /* Notify of the start event */
211: 
212:   sched_note_cpu_start(this_task(), cpu);
213: #endif
214: 
215:   /* Reset Core 1 */
216: 
217:   setbits_reg32(RP2040_PSM_PROC1, RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF);
218:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF) & RP2040_PSM_PROC1))
219:     ;
220:   clrbits_reg32(RP2040_PSM_PROC1, RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF);
221: 
222:   spin_lock(&g_core1_boot);
223: 
224:   /* Send initial VTOR, MSP, PC for Core 1 boot */
225: 
226:   core1_boot_msg[0] = 0;
227:   core1_boot_msg[1] = 1;
228:   core1_boot_msg[2] = getreg32(ARMV6M_SYSCON_VECTAB);
229:   core1_boot_msg[3] = (uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
230:                                 tcb->adj_stack_size;
231:   core1_boot_msg[4] = (uint32_t)core1_boot;
232: 
233:   do
234:     {
235:       fifo_drain();
236:       for (i = 0; i < 5; i++)
237:         {
238:           if (!fifo_comm(core1_boot_msg[i]))
239:             {
240:               break;
241:             }
242:         }
243:     }
244:   while (i < 5);
245: 
246:   fifo_drain();
247: 
248:   /* Enable inter-processor FIFO interrupt */
249: 
250:   irq_attach(RP2040_SMP_CALL_PROC0, rp2040_smp_call_handler, NULL);
251:   up_enable_irq(RP2040_SMP_CALL_PROC0);
252: 
253:   spin_lock(&g_core1_boot);
254: 
255:   /* CPU Core 1 boot done */
256: 
257:   spin_unlock(&g_core1_boot);
258: 
259:   return 0;

145:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion of
146:  *   the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal multitasking,
147:  *   the additional CPUs would be started by calling this function.
148:  *
149:  *   Each CPU is provided the entry point to its IDLE task when started.  A
150:  *   TCB for each CPU's IDLE task has been initialized and placed in the
151:  *   CPU's g_assignedtasks[cpu] list.  No stack has been allocated or
152:  *   initialized.

155:  *   CPU has been started, 1 through (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
156:  *

159:  *         value in the range of one to (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).

171: 
172:   DPRINTF("cpu=%d\n", cpu);

176: 
177:   sched_note_cpu_start(this_task(), cpu);
178: #endif
179: 
180:   /* Reset APP_DSP(cpu) */
181: 
182:   modifyreg32(CXD56_CRG_RESET, 1 << (16 + cpu), 0);
183: 
184:   /* Copy initial stack and reset vector for APP_DSP */
185: 
186:   putreg32((uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
187:                      tcb->adj_stack_size, VECTOR_ISTACK);
188:   putreg32((uint32_t)appdsp_boot, VECTOR_RESETV);
189: 
190:   spin_lock(&g_appdsp_boot);
191: 
192:   /* See 3.13.4.16.3 ADSP Startup */
193: 
194:   /* 2. Clock supply */
195: 
196:   modifyreg32(CXD56_CRG_CK_GATE_AHB, 0, 1 << (16 + cpu));
197: 
198:   /* 3. Clock stop */
199: 
200:   modifyreg32(CXD56_CRG_CK_GATE_AHB, 1 << (16 + cpu), 0);
201: 
202:   /* 4. APP_DSP(cpu) start preparation */
203: 
204:   /* Copy APP_DSP0 settings to all 12 tiles for APP_DSP(cpu)

139:  *   Each CPU is provided the entry point to its IDLE task when started.  A
140:  *   TCB for each CPU's IDLE task has been initialized and placed in the
141:  *   CPU's g_assignedtasks[cpu] list.  No stack has been allocated or
142:  *   initialized.
143:  *
144:  *   The OS initialization logic calls this function repeatedly until each
145:  *   CPU has been started, 1 through (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
146:  *
147:  * Input Parameters:
148:  *   cpu - The index of the CPU being started.  This will be a numeric
149:  *         value in the range of one to (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
150:  *         (CPU 0 is already active)
151:  *
152:  * Returned Value:
153:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
154:  *
155:  ****************************************************************************/
156: 
157: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
158: {
159:   struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(cpu);
160:   uint32_t backup[2];
161: 
162:   DPRINTF("cpu=%d\n", cpu);
163: 
164:   if (cpu != 1)
165:     {
166:       return -1;
167:     }
168: 
169:   /* create initial vectors for CPU1 */
170: 
171:   putreg32(0x1, REMAP); /* remap enable */
172:   backup[0] = getreg32(CPU1_VECTOR_ISTACK);
173:   backup[1] = getreg32(CPU1_VECTOR_RESETV);
174:   putreg32((uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
175:                      tcb->adj_stack_size, CPU1_VECTOR_ISTACK);
176:   putreg32((uint32_t)cpu1_boot, CPU1_VECTOR_RESETV);
177: 
178:   spin_lock(&per_cpu_var_smp(g_cpu_wait, 0));
179: 
180: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION
181:   /* Notify of the start event */
182: 
183:   sched_note_cpu_start(this_task(), cpu);
184: #endif
185: 
186:   /* enable clock core #1 */
187: 
188:   modifyreg32(CORECNT, 0, CORECNT_C1CLKEN);
189: 
190:   /* unreset core #1 */
191: 
192:   modifyreg32(CORECNT, 0, CORECNT_C1RSTN);
193: 
194:   /* IRQ setup CPU1->CPU0 */
195: 
196:   irq_attach(LC823450_IRQ_SMP_CALL_11, lc823450_smp_call_handler, NULL);
197:   up_enable_irq(LC823450_IRQ_SMP_CALL_11);

202:

204:

206:   putreg32(backup[1], CPU1_VECTOR_RESETV);
207:   putreg32(0x0, REMAP); /* remap disable */

74:

85:

101:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion
102:  *   of the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal
103:  *   multitasking, the additional CPUs would be started by calling this
104:  *   function.
105:  *
106:  * Input Parameters:
107:  *   None
108:  *
109:  * Returned Value:
110:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
111:  *
112:  * Assumption:
113:  *   Runs before the full initialization sequence has completed.  Runs after
114:  *   all OS facilities are set up, but before multi-tasking has been started.
115:  *
116:  ****************************************************************************/
117: 
118: int nx_smp_start(void)
119: {
120:   int ret;
121:   int cpu;
122: 
123:   /* Flush dcache before start other CPUs. */
124: 
125:   up_flush_dcache_all();
126:

137:           return ret;
138:         }
139:     }

153: static inline int __spin_lock(volatile spinlock_t *lock)
154: {
155: 	uint32_t core_id;
156: 	int status = 0;
157: 
158: 	// Note: The core IDs are the full 32 bit (CORE_ID_REGVAL_PRO/CORE_ID_REGVAL_APP) values
159: 	core_id = portGET_CORE_ID();
160: 
161: 	// The caller is already the owner of the lock. Simply increment the nesting count
162: 	if (lock->owner == core_id)
163: 	{
164: 		BK_ASSERT(lock->count > 0 && lock->count < 0xFF);	  // Bad count value implies memory corruption
165: 		lock->count ++;
166: 		return 1;
167: 	}
168: 
169: 	do
170: 	{
171: 		// Note: __LDAEX and __STREXW are CMSIS functions
172: 
173: 		while (__LDAEX(&lock->owner) != SPIN_LOCK_FREE)
174: 		{
175: 			__WFE();
176: 		}
177: 
178: 		BK_ASSERT((core_id == 0) || (core_id  == 1));
179: 
180: 		// lock is free
181: 		status = __STREXW(core_id, &lock->owner); // Try to set
182: 
183: 	} while (status != 0); // retry until lock successfully
184: 
185: 	lock->count ++;
186: 
187: 	return 1;
188: }

190: static inline int __spin_lock_try(volatile spinlock_t *lock)
191: {
192: 	uint32_t core_id;
193: 	int status = 0;
194: 
195: 	// Note: The core IDs are the full 32 bit (CORE_ID_REGVAL_PRO/CORE_ID_REGVAL_APP) values
196: 	core_id = portGET_CORE_ID();
197: 
198: 	// The caller is already the owner of the lock. Simply increment the nesting count
199: 	if (lock->owner == core_id)
200: 	{
201: 		BK_ASSERT(lock->count > 0 && lock->count < 0xFF);	  // Bad count value implies memory corruption
202: 		lock->count ++;
203: 		return 1;
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	// Note: __LDAEX and __STREXW are CMSIS functions
207: 
208: 	if (__LDAEX(&lock->owner) != SPIN_LOCK_FREE)
209: 	{
210: 		return 0;
211: 	}
212: 
213: 	BK_ASSERT((core_id == 0) || (core_id  == 1));
214: 	// lock is free
215: 	status = __STREXW(core_id, &lock->owner); // Try to set
216: 
217: 	if(status != 0)
218: 	{
219: 		return 0;
220: 	}
221: 
222: 	lock->count ++;
223:

**Conclusion**

The trace `primary=22, secondary=5` means:

- `primary=22` is `BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_RELEASED`, written immediately after CPU2 reset release in [bk7258_cpustart.c:174-177](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:174).
- `secondary=5` is `BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IDLE`, written at entry to `bk7258_secondary_idle()` in [bk7258_cpustart.c:56-59](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:56).

CPU2 therefore executed through:

```text
secondary_start
  -> private initialization
  -> secondary NVIC initialization
  -> secondary Mailbox initialization
  -> bk7258_secondary_idle entry
```

It did not produce a later marker because there are no markers between stage 5 and the online publication. The failure is in, or immediately after:

```text
arm_initialize_stack()
up_irq_enable()
atomic_set_release(&g_cpu2_online, 1)
bk7258_smp_boot_notify()
```

The strongest concrete defect is that the current code enables CPU2 interrupts before it publishes `g_cpu2_online`.

**Current secondary path**

The exact sequence is [bk7258_cpustart.c:56-65](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:56):

```c
bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IDLE);
arm_initialize_stack();
up_irq_enable();
atomic_set_release(&g_cpu2_online, 1);
bk7258_smp_boot_notify();
sched_note_cpu_started(this_task());
nx_idle_trampoline();
```

This is unsafe during secondary bootstrap because `up_irq_enable()` can immediately deliver:

- a stale or pending Mailbox IRQ 79;
- a pending PendSV/SysTick/system exception not cleared by the secondary setup;
- an interrupt whose handler uses the shared NuttX scheduler or the hwspinlock-backed libc atomic implementation before CPU2 has published itself online.

`bk7258_irqinitialize_secondary()` clears external NVIC pending bits and disables SysTick, but it does not clear all system exception pending state. It then enables the CPU2 Mailbox route in [bk7258_mbox0.c:402-412](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:402).

This ordering differs from original Armino. Armino CPU2 starts with interrupts disabled in [startup_cpu2.c:266-272](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/cmsis/CMSIS_5/Device/Beken/bk7236xx/Source/smp/startup_cpu2.c:266). Its secondary scheduler wrapper also explicitly disables interrupts before starting the scheduler in [port.c:1164-1174](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/port.c:1164). Interrupts are only globally enabled by the first-task assembly path at [portasm.c:161-174](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/portasm.c:161).

The original Armino port also publishes its core-online state from the scheduler startup path, not from an interrupt-enabled pre-scheduler idle entry: [port.c:962-990](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/port.c:962).

**`arm_initialize_stack()`**

The stack setup itself appears structurally correct.

The generic ARMv8-M implementation:

- obtains the per-CPU interrupt stack with `up_get_intstackbase(this_cpu())`;
- computes `stack = stacklim + INTSTACK_SIZE`;
- switches the thread to PSP if necessary;
- installs MSP/MSPLIM for the current CPU.

See [arm_initialstate.c:191-240](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/armv8-m/arm_initialstate.c:191).

Current CPU2 stack allocation is also correct:

- two 2048-byte interrupt stacks are allocated in [bk7258_cpuidlestack.c:15-19](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpuidlestack.c:15);
- CPU1/NuttX logical CPU0 uses the first stack;
- CPU2/NuttX logical CPU1 uses the second stack in [bk7258_cpuidlestack.c:31-35](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpuidlestack.c:31);
- the linker map places the interrupt stack region at `0x2802ac60`, with the CPU2 stack ending at `0x2802bc60`, immediately before the 1 KiB bootstrap stack at `0x2802bc60..0x2802c060`: [nuttx.map:12095](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.map:12095), [nuttx.map:12381](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.map:12381).

The linked disassembly confirms that `arm_initialize_stack()` is entered and switches MSP/MSPLIM as intended. It is not inherently invalid merely because it changes MSP: CPU2 is already running with PSP selected by `bk7258_secondary_enter()` at [bk7258_cpustart.c:68-83](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:68).

The stack path should nevertheless remain before interrupt enable. Do not move `up_irq_enable()` ahead of stack initialization.

**`g_cpu2_online` visibility**

The release/acquire pairing is logically correct:

- CPU2 uses `atomic_set_release()` at [bk7258_cpustart.c:61](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:61).
- CPU1 uses `atomic_read_acquire()` at [bk7258_cpustart.c:180-184](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:180).

This is not a normal lock-free atomic handoff in this build. `CONFIG_LIBC_ATOMIC_HWSPINLOCK=y` is enabled in [defconfig:53](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/defconfig:53). The libc atomic implementation routes every load/store through `g_atomic_hwspinlock` in [arch_atomic.c:324-345](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/libs/libc/machine/arch_atomic.c:324). The linked `atomic_store_4()` therefore:

```text
up_irq_save()
  -> acquire AP_SPINLOCK at 0x28000000
  -> store g_cpu2_online
  -> release AP_SPINLOCK
  -> restore interrupt state
```

The corresponding lock implementation sleeps in `wfe` while the gate is occupied: [bk7258_hwspinlock.c:18-47](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_hwspinlock.c:18).

The shared gate is correctly initialized by the primary in [bk7258_start.c:200-203](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:200), and the AP spinlock region is mapped as shared non-cacheable memory in [bk7258_start.c:60-64](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:60). Thus this is not primarily a cache-visibility error.

However, using the global hwspinlock for a one-writer/one-reader boot flag creates an avoidable bootstrap dependency:

- CPU1 repeatedly performs `atomic_read_acquire()` in a tight loop.
- CPU2 performs a single `atomic_store_release()`.
- Both operations contend on the same non-fair lock.
- The lock implementation uses `wfe`, and the primary’s tight polling loop does not yield or wait.

The minimal robust boot-only implementation would use a dedicated volatile word with explicit barriers rather than the libc atomic API:

```text
primary:
    g_cpu2_online = 0;
    DMB/DSB;

secondary:
    DMB;
    g_cpu2_online = 1;
    DMB/DSB;

primary:
    read g_cpu2_online;
    acquire barrier after observing 1;
```

The existing release/acquire implementation is semantically valid if it completes, but it is a poor primitive for proving CPU2 online during the earliest SMP handoff.

**Minimal ordering fix**

The smallest source change is to keep interrupts disabled until after the online publication and boot notification:

```c
arm_initialize_stack();
atomic_set_release(&g_cpu2_online, 1);
bk7258_smp_boot_notify();
up_irq_enable();
sched_note_cpu_started(this_task());
nx_idle_trampoline();
```

This matches the essential Armino behavior: secondary initialization and online publication occur while interrupts are masked, and interrupt delivery begins only after the core has reached a valid scheduler/idle state.

For a more robust fix, combine that ordering change with a lock-free dedicated boot flag. The ordering change is the first fix to make; replacing the atomic backend removes the remaining possibility that CPU1’s tight acquire polling prevents CPU2’s one-time store from acquiring the shared gate.

**Mailbox raw IPI direction**

The raw Mailbox source/destination mapping is correct and is not the cause of this exact trace.

The current mapping is:

```text
NuttX CPU0 = physical AP CPU1
  channel 1 / CH1
  destination CPU2 = 2

NuttX CPU1 = physical AP CPU2
  channel 2 / CH2
  destination CPU1 = 1
```

Current send logic is [bk7258_mbox0.c:98-133](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:98). Current raw kick destination is `cpu + 1` in [bk7258_smpcall.c:30-50](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:30).

The receive-side source check is also consistent:

- CPU0 expects source `2`;
- CPU1 expects source `1`;

in [bk7258_mbox0.c:254-273](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:254).

That matches Armino:

- `SELF_CHNL` is the physical core endpoint in [mbox0_drv.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.h);
- CPU1-to-CPU2 sends use channel 1 with destination 2;
- CPU2-to-CPU1 sends use channel 2 with destination 1;
- raw messages are identified by `data[1] == 0` in [mbox0_drv.c:51-70](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c:51).

Also, CPU2 cannot have generated the normal boot raw IPI before stage 5 completes: `bk7258_smp_boot_notify()` is after the online store at [bk7258_cpustart.c:61-62](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:61). A source/destination reversal could break the later IPI self-test, but it cannot explain CPU2 failing before publishing online unless a stale Mailbox IRQ/FIFO entry is being serviced.

**Timer dependence**

CPU2 correctly does not initialize a second SysTick. The current secondary path has no `up_timer_initialize()` call. That agrees with the SMP porting plan’s requirement that only logical CPU0 owns the NuttX system timer: [BK7258_OPENVELA_SMP_PORTING_PLAN.md:751-753](/home/mi/vela_competition/BK7258_OPENVELA_SMP_PORTING_PLAN.md:751).

The primary timer is initialized through [bk7258_timerisr.c:13-17](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:13), using the architecture timer lower half. `clock_systime_ticks()` reads that timer through `up_timer_gettick()` in [clock_systime_ticks.c:79-95](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/clock/clock_systime_ticks.c:79).

The primary timeout before CPU2 becomes online is therefore valid only if CPU0’s SysTick is already running. In this build it should be: `nx_start()` calls `up_initialize()` before `nx_smp_start()` in [nx_start.c:706-718](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/init/nx_start.c:706), and SMP startup follows at [nx_start.c:805-813](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/init/nx_start.c:805).

There is a separate timeout defect after CPU2 becomes visible. The inner loop uses unbounded `wfe`:

```c
while (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete() &&
